items.inputs: Total 03 Non-Conformance were found.
items.outputs: All non-conformities (NCs) identified during the internal audit should be completed within one-week timeframe. Individual deadlines have been assigned for each NC/Observation. However, the ultimate deadline for closing all NCs is set for 30th July 2024.
items.resources: Will be mentioned below where needed.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 7.1 regarding the Resource Management. The non-conformance occurred due to uncontrolled environmental conditions.
items.outputs: It is decided that Flap Door will be used to separate Laboratory area from workstation and door pads will be used to close the slits below door for controlling cold loss from air-conditioning system which is available for maintaining the controlled environmental conditions.

items.inputs:
NC for clause # 7.4 regarding the Communication.
The " Communication log” ETAL-IMS-700-FF-05 for IMS planning exists but has not been properly implemented.
items.outputs: The MR is responsible to draft a document to determine the cause of the issue and outline corrective action to fix it. The record of “communication log” ETAL-IMS-700-FF-05 should be properly updated as per plan.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.4 regarding the Control of externally provided processes, products and services. The List of External provided services (ETAL-IMS-800-FF-02) was not updated.
items.outputs: The MR is responsible to draft a document to determine the cause of the issue and outline corrective action to fix it. The document of “List of External provided services” ETAL-IMS-800-FF-02 should be properly updated as per plan.

items.inputs: The inventory record of chemicals and other requirements was reviewed & discussed.
items.outputs: Enlisting of expiring chemicals and nearly expiring certificates will be renewed from AIMS and Delta, Procurement of requirements will be done.

items.inputs: New Methods will be developed for COD and TOC analysis.
items.outputs: The Plan was discussed, and it mutually decided for development of both methods. Procurement of all relevant required chemicals, equipment and accessories will be done by administration. Assistant Lab Manager will be responsible for method development.

circular.venue: Lahore Office (Video Conferencing with Top Management)
circular.subject: Management Review Meeting
circular.intro: I am pleased to inform all of you that the Management Review Meeting on Internal Audit and ISO/IEC 17025:2017 will be held on 24-Feb-2025. This MRM must be performed to discuss the ISO Clause status of ISO 17025:2017 Compliance within your respective departments.
agenda: Changes in internal and external issues that are relevant to the laboratory.

minutes.file: ETAL-QMS-809-FF-02  Mintues of Management Review Meeting with Amendments.docx

items.inputs: Total 08 Non-Conformance were found.
items.outputs: All non-conformities (NCs) identified during the internal audit should be completed within eight-week timeframe. Individual deadlines have been assigned for each NC/Observation. However, the ultimate deadline for closing all NCs is set for 15th April 2025 except the NC of CRM.
items.resources: Resources are noted for each NC where applicable.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 4.1 regarding Impartiality occurred due to the unavailability of Undertaking of laboratory personnel for Impartiality on stamp paper.
items.outputs: It has been decided that stamp papers will be procured to obtain signed Impartiality Undertakings, ensuring the document is legally binding.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 4.2 regarding confidentiality occurred due to the unavailability of Undertaking of laboratory personnel for the confidentiality on stamp paper.
items.outputs: It has been decided that stamp papers will be procured to obtain signed confidentiality Undertakings, ensuring the document is legally binding.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 6.3 regarding Facilities and environmental conditions. The records of environmental condition graphs (ETAL-LAB-603-FF-07, ETAL-LAB-603-FF-07A, and ETAL-LAB-603-FF-07B) were not updated as required by 6.3.4 for periodical review of data.
items.outputs: It has been decided that environmental condition graphs (ETAL-LAB-603-FF-07, ETAL-LAB-603-FF-07A, and ETAL-LAB-603-FF-07B) will be prepared monthly using data from monthly logs. Additionally, the records for the period of November 2024 to January 2025 will be completed retrospectively.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 6.4 regarding the Equipment. The non-conformance was identified due to the Master List of Lab Equipment (ETAL-LAB-604-FF-15) not being updated as required.
items.outputs: The Management Representative (MR) is responsible for preparing a document to determine the root cause and define appropriate corrective actions. The Master List (ETAL-LAB-604-FF-15) will be updated accordingly to ensure accuracy and compliance with the documented plan.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 6.5 regarding Metrological Traceability. Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) are not available.
items.outputs: The laboratory will identify and list the required CRMs and initiate the procurement process to ensure compliance with metrological traceability requirements. To meet standard requirements, CRMs will be imported through a Certified Supplier (e.g. LSS) to ensure traceability and compliance.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 7.6 regarding Evaluation of measurement uncertainty. The non-conformance was raised due to inconsistent evaluation and lack of documentation of measurement uncertainty (MU) results, as required by procedure ETAL-LAB-P-706.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the laboratory will conduct training sessions on MU evaluation for relevant staff and ensure that MU calculations are performed and documented for all applicable test methods. Records will be maintained as per the defined procedure to demonstrate compliance.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 7.7 regarding Ensuring the validity of results. Lab needs to use CRM for assurance of its test results.
items.outputs: The laboratory will identify and list the required CRMs, initiate their procurement, and ensure traceability by importing CRMs through a certified supplier (e.g., LSS). This action will support compliance with standard requirements and enhance the reliability of test results.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.5 regarding Actions to address risks and opportunities (Option A). The non-conformance was identified as the laboratory has not identified or documented the risks and opportunities associated with its activities, as required by the standard.
items.outputs: To address this, the laboratory will implement a systematic approach to assess, document, and monitor risks and opportunities to ensure continual improvement and compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.5 regarding Improvement (Option A). The non-conformance was raised as the laboratory has not prepared an Improvement Analysis report.
items.outputs: The management decided based on available customer feedback forms that the laboratory will initiate the Improvement Analysis process starting from the year 2025. Due to limited customer feedback data available so far, a comprehensive report could not be developed previously.

items.inputs: Actions identified during the previous MRM, including the IMS Audit, EPD Audit, and method development for COD and TOC has been discussed.
items.outputs:
The following actions have been completed and found effective: IMS Audit, EPD Audit and Method Development for COD
Pending Action Identified:
The Method Development for TOC has not achieved the desired outcomes and is considered an unsuccessful project. Further review and corrective planning are required.

items.inputs: Installation of Fume hood
items.outputs: Successful installation of the fume hood has been completed to effectively control and manage laboratory fumes, enhancing workplace safety and compliance with environmental conditions.

items.inputs: In the last week, laboratory personnel participated in external training organized by ETAL and conducted by Mr. Imtiaz from AIMS on ISO/IEC 17025:2017.
items.outputs: The training covered key areas such as management system requirements, technical competence, measurement uncertainty, internal audits, and reporting of results. Participation certificates were issued, and training records have been updated accordingly in ETAL-LAB-602-FF-04 (Training Record). This initiative enhanced understanding of standard requirements and strengthened implementation across all lab operations.

items.inputs: Quality Objectives are identified and enlisted for Year 2025.
items.outputs: Quality objectives for the year 2025 have been identified, documented, and enlisted in accordance with the laboratory's quality management system. These objectives are aligned with the lab's strategic direction and are being monitored for implementation and effectiveness (Ref: ETAL-QMS-802-FF-02).

addendum.outputs: Approved updates to existing SOPs and policies.

addendum.inputs: PNAC Surveillance Assessment was conducted on 16th April 2025, with an overall satisfactory outcome. Observations were noted regarding the organogram, impartiality and confidentiality undertakings, risk and opportunity records, approval dates, improvement documentation, internal audit witnessing, and inclusion of relevant clauses in MRM minutes.
addendum.outputs:
Assigned responsible personnel to address all PNAC observations with targeted deadlines.
Update ETAL organogram and approval dates in relevant documents.
Obtaining Undertakings on impartiality and confidentiality from concern personnel.
Approval for Revision and documentation of Risk and opportunity assessment records.
Improvement documentation reviewed and aligned with current practices.
Instructed to plan Witnessing of testing activities to align with Internal Audit.
Directed inclusion of specific clause references in future MRM minutes for compliance tracking.

Document Control Access – To update the organogram, approval dates, and manage version control of revised documents.

HR and Admin Support – For obtaining signed undertakings on impartiality and confidentiality from concerned personnel.

Quality Assurance Personnel – To review, revise, and align improvement-related documentation.

addendum.agenda: Changes in the volume and type of work or in the range of laboratory activities
addendum.inputs: Preparation initiated for expanding scope to include vehicular emissions testing using NDIR-based CO analyzers; Stack emission using Iso-kinetic assembly.
addendum.outputs: Initiated procurement of equipment and SOP development for vehicular emission testing (CO analyzers) and Stack emission.

addendum.inputs: Customer feedback were generally positive, emphasizing timely reporting and the professionalism of field teams, with a few suggestions for faster result turnaround and improved communication regarding sample status.
addendum.outputs: Management acknowledged the feedback and directed improvements in communication protocols and result turnaround time. IT was tasked with exploring options for enhancing client communication channels, and QA was asked to review processes for timely reporting.
addendum.resources: IT support for communication system upgrades, QA team involvement to optimize reporting processes, staff training, and budget for software enhancements.

addendum.inputs: No formal complaints were received from clients or stakeholders during the review period, indicating general satisfaction with the services provided.
addendum.outputs: Management acknowledged the absence of complaints as a positive indicator of service quality and directed continued adherence to established procedures and proactive client engagement to maintain satisfaction levels.
addendum.resources:
Existing client feedback and communication channels

Monitoring tools for capturing and tracking any future complaints

Continued staff training to maintain service quality

addendum.inputs: During the review period, several improvements were implemented, including the enhancement of reporting processes through reporting software and the installation of a fume hood. These actions led to reduced reporting time, minimized errors, and enhanced client satisfaction, demonstrating the effectiveness of the implemented measures.
addendum.outputs: Management acknowledged the positive impact of recent improvements and directed continued monitoring of performance indicators. It was decided to document lessons learned, maintain improvement momentum, and identify further areas where process efficiency and safety can be enhanced.
addendum.resources:
Performance monitoring tools (KPIs, client feedback records)

Technical support for reporting software maintenance

Safety and maintenance resources for fume hood operation
addendum.responsibility:
IT Support to maintain and troubleshoot reporting software.

Lab Supervisor to ensure proper use and upkeep of the fume hood.
Management to review improvement outcomes and guide further initiatives.

addendum.inputs: Current resources were reviewed and found generally adequate for routine laboratory operations. However, increased demand and expanded testing scope (e.g., Metal analysis including Sodium and Potassium) highlighted the need for relevant Lamps and Standards.
addendum.outputs: Management acknowledged that current resources adequately support routine operations but recognized the need to acquire additional lamps and standards for metal analysis, including sodium and potassium.
addendum.resources: Procurement of specific lamps and certified reference standards for metal analysis (sodium and potassium), budget allocation for purchases, and technical support for installation and calibration.

addendum.inputs:
The recent risk identification exercise highlighted a range of potential risks impacting laboratory operations and quality, including:
Chemical hazards related to acids and solvents handling.
Risks in sample handling, storage, contamination, and mislabelling.
Laboratory facility access control and environmental factors such as warm lighting, temperature fluctuations, humidity, and extended electricity failures.
Personnel-related risks such as conflicts of interest, undue influence, undefined roles, testing beyond competence, and technical knowledge gaps.
Data integrity risks including breach of confidentiality, reporting errors, data loss, and unauthorized access.
Equipment-related risks like malfunction, calibration lapses, and use of non-traceable standards.
Quality risks from poor reagents, subcontracted services, non-validated methods, and misestimation of uncertainty.
Operational risks including recurrence of non-conformities, ineffective management oversight, poor proficiency testing participation, cross-document inconsistencies, and misapplication of statistical techniques.
Mitigation strategies have been prioritized to address these risks through updated procedures, training, improved monitoring, and enhanced management controls.
addendum.outputs: Management reviewed the identified risks and approved the implementation of targeted mitigation measures, including staff training on chemical and sample handling, enhanced calibration and maintenance schedules, access control reinforcement, and improved data security protocols. MR was directed to update the risk register and monitor mitigation effectiveness as part of ongoing internal audits.
addendum.resources:
Updated risk register and assessment tools

Training materials for staff on risk mitigation (e.g., chemical handling, data security, sample management)

IT supports data security and access control improvements

QA oversight for monitoring risk controls
addendum.responsibility:
QA Team to update the risk register and verify effectiveness of mitigation actions
Lab Manager to coordinate staff training and enforce SOP adherence
Technical Staff to ensure timely calibration and equipment servicing

IT Department to implement and monitor data security measures
Management to oversee risk mitigation progress and allocate required resources

addendum.agenda: Outcomes of the Assurance of the validity of results
addendum.inputs: Validity of results was assured through successful participation in proficiency testing schemes, routine quality control checks, and method validation exercises. Control charts remained within acceptable limits, internal audits confirmed procedural compliance, and no critical discrepancies were reported in duplicate or blind sample analyses.
addendum.outputs: Management acknowledged the effectiveness of current quality assurance measures in maintaining result validity. It was directed to continue participation in proficiency testing, strengthen internal audits, and ensure regular review of quality control data. The QA team was instructed to identify any trends and initiate early corrective actions if deviations occur.
addendum.resources:
Proficiency Testing (PT) schemes
Internal quality control materials (e.g., control samples, reference standards)
Trained QA personnel for audits and data review

circular.file: ETAL-QMS-809-FF-01  Circular of Management Review Meeting-2026.docx
circular.subject: Management Review Meeting
circular.intro: I am pleased to inform all of you that the Management Review Meeting on Internal Audit of ISO 17025:2017 will be held on 09th March 2026. This MRM must be performed to discuss the ISO Clause status of ISO 17025:2017 Compliance within your respective departments.
agenda: Changes in internal and external issues that are relevant to the laboratory.

minutes.file: ETAL-QMS-809-FF-02  Minutes of Management Review Meeting.docx

items.inputs: Total 09 Non-Conformance were found.
items.outputs: All non-conformities (NCs) identified during the internal audit should be completed within eight-week timeframe. Individual deadlines have been assigned for each NC/Observation. However, the ultimate deadline for closing all NCs is set for 23rd April 2026.
items.resources: Resources are noted for each NC where applicable.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 4.1 regarding Impartiality occurred due to the unavailability of residual risks in Risk Assessment Form (ETAL-QMS-805-FF-01), and acceptance criteria for residual risks has not been defined by the lab.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the laboratory will revise the Risk Assessment Procedure (ETAL-QMS-805-P) and Risk Assessment Form (ETAL-QMS-805-FF-01) to incorporate a structured section for evaluating risks after implementation of control measures, along with clearly defined acceptance criteria. The procedure will be updated to ensure systematic evaluation of the effectiveness of risk controls in accordance with Clause 8.5 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017, and all existing risk assessments will be reviewed and updated accordingly.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 4.1 regarding Impartiality occurred because impartiality declarations were not formally extended to committee members, contractors, and external representatives, as the laboratory considered existing organizational controls such as supervision, hierarchy, and internal review processes to be sufficient to safeguard impartiality
items.outputs: It has been decided that the laboratory will revise the format of the Impartiality Undertaking (ETAL-QMS-401-FF-01) into a single standardized form applicable to all categories, including personnel, committee members, contractors, external bodies, and visitors. The Impartiality Procedure (ETAL-QMS-P-401) will be updated accordingly to reflect this change and ensure consistent implementation.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 4.2 regarding confidentiality occurred because confidentiality undertakings were issued only to internal staff, contractors, and service providers, and not extended to committee members or external representatives.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the laboratory will revise the format of the Confidentiality Undertaking (ETAL-QMS-402-FF-01) into a single standardized form applicable to all categories, including personnel, committee members, contractors, external bodies, and visitors. The Confidentiality Procedure (ETAL-QMS-P-402) will be updated accordingly to reflect this change and ensure consistent implementation.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 6.3 regarding Facilities and environmental conditions. The facilities like, equipment, fitting/fixtures, electric supply, gas supply, water supply, storage of Lab equipment /test items are not defined and documented, as and when required for carrying out testing activities.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the laboratory will revise the Procedure of “Facilities and Environmental Conditions (ETAL-LAB-P-603) to include and clearly document all facilities available in the laboratory, including electricity supply, gas supply, DI water system, equipment, storage areas, and fittings & fixtures.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 6.3 regarding Facilities and environmental conditions. Equipment ID is not mentioned in log sheet and correction factor of hygrometer is also not incorporated in log sheet neither in control chart.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the “ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITION LOG (LAB) -(ETAL-LAB-603-FF-01A)” format shall be revised to include dedicated fields for recording both the observed value and the value after application of the correction factor. The correction factor shall be applied as per the calibration certificate of the hygrometer or weather station. All corrected values shall be utilized for plotting in control charts to ensure accurate trend analysis. Furthermore, the log sheet shall be updated to include a mandatory provision for recording the instrument identification to ensure complete traceability.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 6.4 regarding the Equipment. The non-conformance was identified because independent monthly intermediate check data are not being plotted on the control chart for ongoing monitoring.
items.outputs: The laboratory will revise its balance monitoring practice to ensure that independent monthly verification data recorded in ANALYTICAL BALANCE IN-HOUSE CALIBRATION CHECK LOG (ETAL-LAB-FF-604-01) are incorporated into the control chart format ETAL-LAB-604-FF-11A, along with the baseline established from intermediate check results. All relevant historical monthly check data will be reviewed, compiled, and plotted to develop a complete and representative control chart.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 7.7 regarding Validity of Results. The nonconformity occurred because the test method does not provide guidance for pre-adjustment or verification of sample volume prior to analysis to ensure the residue falls within 2.5 mg to 200 mg.
items.outputs: The laboratory will introduce a pre-analysis verification step for sample volume selection to ensure the expected result falls within the required measurement range before testing. A calculation/check step will be incorporated into the "Lab Instruction for total dissolve solids " (ETAL-LAB-702-FF-03 (TDS)" to confirm appropriate sample volume prior to analysis.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 7.8 regarding Reporting of results. The non-conformance was raised because The Customer Request Form was not adequately reviewed for alignment with current laboratory reporting practices, resulting in the continued inclusion of "Opinions and Interpretations" despite their exclusion from laboratory activities.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the customer request form will be revised (ETAL-LAB-708-FF-17) to remove references to opinions and interpretations and align it with laboratory policy.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 7.11 regarding Data and information control. The laboratory has not established a dedicated procedure to address data and information management requirements.
items.outputs: The laboratory will develop a new procedure for “Control Data & Information Management System ETAL-QMS-P-711” in line with Clause 7.11 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017. This procedure will define who can access data, how software/LIMS is validated and how data is protected through passwords and backups. It will also cover control of external systems, and reference data for staff, and proper checking of calculations and data transfers with documented evidence.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.2 regarding Management System Documentation. The non-conformance was identified as the laboratory has not ensured effective communication and implementation of objectives at all levels.
items.outputs: To address this, the laboratory will revise and update the format of Quality Objectives (ETAL-QMS-802-FF-02) to ensure clear definition, assignment, and documentation of responsibilities.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.3 regarding control of management system. The non-conformance was raised as the laboratory was already implementing document preparation, review, and approval in routine practice; however, these responsibilities were not explicitly described in the document control procedure.
items.outputs: It has been decided that the laboratory will revise the “Procedure for Control of Management System Documents” (ETAL-QMS-P-803) to clearly define the responsibilities for document preparation, review, and approval, ensuring alignment between actual practices and documented requirements.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.3 regarding control of management system. The non-conformance was raised because the document control procedure does not establish a standardized first-page format across all document levels (Level I–IV), although documents within each category (policies, procedures, and forms/formats) follow consistent internal formats.
items.outputs: To address this, the procedure for “Procedure for Control of Management System Documents” (ETAL-QMS-P-803) will be revised and updated to establish a standardized formatting style for all document levels (Level I–IV).

items.inputs:
NC for clause # 8.4 regarding control of Records (Option A). The non-conformance was raised because the existing procedures Technical Record (ETAL-LAB-P-705, & Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803 did not comprehensively address the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.4 for control of records.
Lab has described the retention period for records as three years: lab needs to rectify its statement about the retention period as the retention period also depends on legal obligations.
items.outputs:
To address this, the laboratory shall revise the Control of “Procedure for Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803 “to incorporate a dedicated section addressing the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.4 (Control of Records).
The laboratory will revise the Procedure for Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803 to ensure record retention periods are defined based on applicable legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements instead of a fixed duration

items.inputs: Actions identified during the previous MRM, including the ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Audit, IMS Audit, and PT Participation for the year 2026 have been discussed.
items.outputs: The following actions have been completed and found effective: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Audit, IMS Audit and PT Participation in Round 2026-02.

items.inputs: Replacement of Filters of water DI system have been discussed.

circular.subject: Management Review Meeting
circular.intro: I am pleased to inform all concerned that the Management Review Meeting for Review of Laboratory Procedures in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 will be held on 03-Sep-2025. This MRM is conducted to review the effectiveness, suitability, and continued applicability of laboratory management system and technical procedures within their respective functional areas, ensuring compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 requirements and current laboratory practices.
agenda: Review of Laboratory Procedures (Management System and Technical Procedures)
Assessment of Procedure Suitability, Adequacy, and Effectiveness
Verification of Alignment of Procedures with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Requirements
Review of Implementation Status of Procedures in Laboratory Operations
Identification of Any Required Updates or Improvements in Procedures
Confirmation of Document Control Status (Issue Date, Revision No., Issue No.)
Verification of Periodic Review Compliance of Procedures
Any Other Relevant Matters Related to Procedure Implementation and Control

items.inputs: The Management Review Meeting included a comprehensive review of all laboratory management system and technical procedures that had completed the defined periodic review cycle of three (3) years, in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 requirements for document control and periodic review. The objective of this review was to ensure that each procedure remains suitable, adequate, and effectively implemented in line with current laboratory operations and regulatory requirements. Each procedure was evaluated for its continued relevance, clarity, and effectiveness. All applicable procedures were reviewed one by one to assess their alignment with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 requirements and current laboratory practices.
items.outputs: It was agreed that each procedure shall be evaluated individually for suitability, adequacy, and compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 requirements and current laboratory practices. Where no changes in content are identified during the review, the existing Issue Date, Revision Number, and Issue Number will remain unchanged in accordance with the document control procedure. Where any changes in content are identified, the procedure will be revised accordingly, and a new Issue Date along with updated Revision and Issue Numbers will be assigned as per the document control procedure. The review process will be recorded as evidence of periodic document review under the laboratory quality management system.

items.inputs: The procedure was critically reviewed to evaluate the identification, assessment, and control of risks to impartiality. The effectiveness of implemented controls and management commitment towards impartiality were assessed against ISO/IEC 17025:2017 requirements.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate, effectively implemented, and compliant. No revision required.

items.inputs: The organizational structure defined in the procedure was reviewed to confirm clarity of roles, responsibilities, authorities, and reporting lines. Alignment with current operational structure was verified.
items.outputs: Procedure found suitable and aligned with current organizational setup. No changes required.

items.inputs: The procedure was evaluated with respect to personnel competence, qualification criteria, training processes, and authorization requirements. Implementation effectiveness and compliance with competence requirements were verified.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate and effectively implemented. No revision required.

items.inputs: The procedure was reviewed to assess controls related to equipment selection, calibration, maintenance, verification, and handling. Records and implementation practices were evaluated for compliance.
items.outputs: Procedure found effective and properly implemented. No changes required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-LAB-P-606 (Externally Provided Products & Services)
items.inputs: The supplier evaluation, selection, and monitoring processes were reviewed, including criteria for approval and performance evaluation of external providers.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate and effectively implemented. No revision required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-QMS-P-607 (External & PNAC Audit Handling)
items.inputs: The procedure was reviewed to verify the effectiveness of planning, coordination, and handling of external and accreditation audits, including response to audit findings.
items.outputs: Procedure found suitable and effective. No changes required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-LAB-P-701 (Review of Requests, Tenders & Contracts)
items.inputs: The process for reviewing customer requirements, contract acceptance, and ensuring capability prior to commitment was evaluated for adequacy and implementation.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate and effectively implemented. No revision required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-LAB-P-702 (Method Selection, Verification & Validation)
items.inputs: The procedure was assessed for compliance with method selection, verification, and validation requirements. Implementation practices and records were reviewed for adequacy.
items.outputs: Procedure found effective and compliant. No changes required.

items.inputs: The procedure governing generation, handling, storage, and traceability of technical records was reviewed to ensure data integrity and completeness.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate and effectively implemented. No revision required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-QMS-P-710 (Nonconforming Work & Corrective Action)
items.inputs: The procedure was evaluated for identification, control, and correction of nonconforming work, including root cause analysis and effectiveness of corrective actions.
items.outputs: Procedure found effective and properly implemented. No changes required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-QMS-P-802 (Management System Documentation)
items.inputs: The structure and control of management system documentation were reviewed, including document hierarchy, accessibility, and consistency.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate and suitable. No revision required.

items.agenda: Review of Procedure ETAL-QMS-P-803 (Control of Documents)
items.inputs: The document control process was reviewed, including approval, issuance, revision control, and withdrawal of obsolete documents.
items.outputs: Procedure found effective and properly implemented. No changes required.

items.inputs: The procedure was reviewed to assess identification, evaluation, and mitigation of risks and opportunities, including effectiveness of controls and documentation practices.
items.outputs: Procedure found suitable and effective. No revision required.

items.inputs: The internal audit process was reviewed for planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up of audit findings. Effectiveness of audit implementation was verified.
items.outputs: Procedure found effective and compliant. No changes required.

items.inputs: The management review process was evaluated to ensure adequacy of inputs, outputs, and alignment with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 requirements.
items.outputs: Procedure found adequate and effectively implemented. No revision required.

items.inputs: The prior MRM report was carefully evaluated to ensure that all discussed items were effectively implemented.
items.outputs: It was confirmed that all action items from the previous MRM were successfully completed ahead of their respective target dates. Additionally, all identified non-conformities (NCs) were thoroughly addressed, with appropriate corrective actions implemented and verified for effectiveness, ensuring full closure.
items.resources: Will be discussed point by point where needed.

items.outputs:
It was mutually agreed that all non-conformities (NCs) identified during the internal audit would be resolved within a 1.5-week timeframe. While specific deadlines have been assigned to each NC, the final deadline for closing all NCs is set for
06-Jan- 2026.
items.resources: Will be mentioned below where needed.

items.inputs:
NC-01 (Clause 8.5 – Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities):
During the review of the risk assessment records, it was observed that the laboratory has established the Risk Assessment Procedure (ETAL-QMS-P-805) and maintains records of risks and opportunities using form ETAL-QMS-805-FF-01. However, the documented records do not include information demonstrating the effectiveness of the implemented controls, nor do they specify the person responsible for the closure of identified risks.
items.outputs: The Manager Lab will prepare a detailed report to identify the root cause of the issue and implement appropriate corrective actions. Additionally, Lab Manager will revise the risk assessment document (ETAL-QMS-805-FF-01) to include fields for recording the effectiveness of implemented controls and for specifying the person responsible for closing each identified risk.

items.inputs: NC for clause # 8.6.1 regarding the that other opportunities for improvement arising from sources such as internal audits, management review, complaints, nonconformities, and staff suggestions were not systematically identified, reviewed, or documented. This indicates that the laboratory has not fully implemented a process to identify and review opportunities for improvement from all relevant sources as required by ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.6.1.
items.outputs: The Lab Manager will evaluated the root cause of the issue and initiated corrective actions to address the gap identified under Clause 8.6.1. A standardized format for recording and reviewing opportunities for improvement will be developed and implemented. This format captures inputs from various sources, including internal audits, management reviews, complaints, nonconformities, feedback, and staff suggestions. The Lab Manager has ensured that all identified opportunities are documented in a consolidated manner, systematically reviewed at defined intervals, and analyzed for trends. This approach facilitates effective monitoring and supports continual improvement in compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.6.1.
